metadata.note: User asked for a 'CLI Explainer' by name, documenting this specific week's work — a NEW recap, separate from this user's earlier 'weekly-recap' project (which covered a different week: the ai-nonprofit-marketing article + Suffolk University talk). Built in its own folder (weekly-recap-catbot) rather than overwriting that prior build. Same REQUIRED story spine as that earlier build (B00 cold open -> PROBLEM -> ASK -> CODE -> OUTPUT -> CHANGE -> CODE -> OUTPUT -> SUMMARY -> NEXT STEPS -> OUTRO, real code shown via ClaudeCodeBeat, one required revision cycle), with the same two disclosed substitutions carried forward: (1) voice/branding — af_bella + @HumanitariansAI instead of the skill's default Teardown/am_onyx/@NikBearBrown, per explicit user request for a woman's voice; (2) render pipeline — the skill's documented `vox_run.sh`/`vox_compile.py`/`type_check.py` do not exist anywhere in this toolkit install (re-verified for this build); rendered instead through the same run.sh/compile.py/static_scene_check.py/manim_layout_audit.py/final_frame_check.py pipeline used on every other reel this session. Self-introduction ('Hi, I'm Agrima') stays folded into B00's narration rather than split into its own B00B beat, matching the ORIGINAL weekly-recap's precedent (this is the cli-explainer skill's own reference-example convention: persona name + tagline directly in the cold open) -- distinct from the B00B pattern used on this user's ai-explainer-chassis builds (death-of-the-generic-resume, ai-nonprofit-marketing, rescue-reinvented), which is a different skill with a different convention. The CLI loop's 'build' is real: weekly_recap_v1.py and weekly_recap_v2.py are genuine Python scripts, both actually run (not invented) to capture the CODE/OUTPUT beats' real source and output -- v1 is a flat, undifferentiated list of the week's three items; v2 splits them into DONE THIS WEEK vs STARTING NEXT WEEK, resolving the user's own stated revision-prompt concern (#5: clearly separate 'done this week' from 'just starting') from the FIRST cut, not as a correction. This week's three items, as given in the kickoff: (1) writing -- published 'Rescue, Reinvented: How Artificial Intelligence Is Reshaping Rescue Work' on Substack; (2) video production -- two Brutalist videos produced this week (the rescue-work explainer itself, built earlier this session, and this recap), both worked through the full 16:9+9:16 pipeline; (3) meetings & new research -- discussions of a new 'cat bot' project idea, with early cat-shelter research just starting. Items 1+2 are DONE; item 3 is STARTING NEXT. Three generated visuals were built fresh for this cut per the user's explicit request: a mock article-header card (browser-style dots + headline + kicker) for the Substack piece, a two-aspect-ratio video-production card (overlapping 16:9/9:16 frames + play icon) for the video work, and a cat-bot card (a simple geometric cat silhouette paired with a chat-bubble icon) for the new research direction -- no stock footage or screen recording used; the user was told in this same reply that a real screenshot of the published article or a Brutalist terminal session could later replace either generated card if they want more literal proof, but neither is required for this build. All content is the user's own self-reported work log, not third-party sourced claims -- see FACTCHECK.md.

beats.narration_text: Most weekly updates are a highlight reel — the wins, dressed up. I wanted something closer to a real log: what actually got done, kept separate from what's just getting started.
beats.visual_intent: title card: 'a real log, not a highlight reel' — no composer yet

beats.narration_text: Start simple: ask Claude for a script that just logs the week — the article, the two videos, the cat bot meetings — one flat list, nothing fancy yet.

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL generated code, trimmed to what teaches; weekly_recap_v1.py was really run
beats.narration_text: Here's what it wrote — a flat list, three entries, no ranking, no spin. Just: published this, produced these, and what's starting to take shape.

props.title: weekly_recap_v1.py
props.code:
WEEK = [
    {"item": "Published 'Rescue, Reinvented' on Substack",
     "where": "AI's real impact in animal shelters"},
    {"item": "Produced two Brutalist videos (16:9 + 9:16)",
     "where": "the rescue-work explainer + this recap"},
    {"item": "New project idea: a 'cat bot' -- research started",
     "where": "from this week's meetings"},
]

def log():
    for entry in WEEK:
        print(f"- {entry['item']}  ({entry['where']})")

beats.role_note: OPEN vox slot -> Manim video; the real weekly_recap_v1.py output, visualized as three same-weight cards
beats.narration_text: Run it, and here's the week: 'Rescue, Reinvented,' published on Substack — AI actually helping shelters. Two Brutalist videos, produced start to finish, both formats. And a new idea from this week's meetings: a cat bot, with early shelter research already underway. All three, same weight.
beats.visual_intent: Manim: three cards in a flat row — a mock article-header card ('Rescue, Reinvented'), a two-aspect-ratio video-production card (16:9 + 9:16 overlapping frames), and a cat-bot card (cat silhouette + chat bubble) — all the same visual weight, undifferentiated

beats.narration_text: That's the problem, though — a flat list treats 'I published an article' the same as 'I'm still researching cat shelters.' So: revise it. Split what's actually finished from what's just beginning.

props.command:
claude "update weekly_recap_v1.py -> weekly_recap_v2.py:
  -> split into DONE THIS WEEK vs STARTING NEXT WEEK"
props.segment: This Week: What Shipped, What's Next

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the revised code; weekly_recap_v2.py was really run
beats.narration_text: Same week, same three items — now in two lists. Done: the article, the videos. Next: the cat bot idea, and the research that's just starting.

props.title: weekly_recap_v2.py
props.code:
DONE = [
    {"item": "Published 'Rescue, Reinvented' on Substack",
     "where": "AI's real impact in animal shelters"},
    {"item": "Produced two Brutalist videos (16:9 + 9:16)",
     "where": "the rescue-work explainer + this recap"},
]

NEXT = [
    {"item": "New project idea: a 'cat bot'",
     "where": "cat-shelter research just starting"},
]

def log():
    print("DONE THIS WEEK")
    ...
    print("STARTING NEXT WEEK")
    ...

beats.role_note: OPEN vox slot -> Manim video; the real weekly_recap_v2.py output, visualized as a DONE/NEXT split
beats.narration_text: Re-run it, and the shape changes completely. Done this week: 'Rescue, Reinvented' is published, and both videos are actually finished, in both formats. Starting next: the cat bot — a new project idea from this week's meetings, plus early cat-shelter research. Nothing here is finished yet — that's the point of saying so.
beats.visual_intent: Manim: the same three cards, now regrouped under two headers — DONE THIS WEEK (checkmark, good-green) holding the article + video cards; STARTING NEXT WEEK (arrow, terracotta) holding the cat-bot card — a vertical divider between the two groups

beats.narration_text: So that's the real log: one article shipped, two videos actually produced, and one new idea — the cat bot — just getting its first research. Separating done from next isn't a small detail. It's the difference between a recap and a highlight reel.
beats.visual_intent: recap card: 'done' vs 'next' reframed as the actual lesson, not just a formatting choice
